title: First transmission
summary: A message from the dunes. One familiar encoding.
description: The field team left a text transmission. Recover the flag from the supplied file.
hint: An alphabet ending with = often signals Base64.

title: Shift change
summary: The alphabet has moved. The message has not.
description: An operator rotated every letter by the same amount. Digits and punctuation were left unchanged. Find the rotation.
hint: Try all 26 Caesar shifts; the flag starts with FALCON{.

title: Repeating horizon
summary: A short key keeps coming around.
description: The bytes were encrypted with repeating-key XOR. The key is five bytes long. You know the flag prefix.
hint: XOR the first five ciphertext bytes with FALCO to recover the key.

title: One pad, two messages
summary: Two intercepted messages share one fatal mistake.
description: Both messages used the same stream of random bytes with XOR, starting at offset zero. A weather report is known. Recover the other plaintext.
hint: C1 XOR P1 recovers the keystream; apply the first needed bytes to C2.

title: Shared foundations
summary: Two RSA keys were built on common ground.
description: Two RSA public keys accidentally share a prime. The flag is a big-endian integer encrypted under n1 with textbook RSA. Recover it.
hint: Compute gcd(n1,n2). Then calculate the private exponent modulo (p−1)(q−1).

title: Two seals
summary: Different exponents. The same hidden message.
description: Two operators encrypted the same flag using the same RSA modulus but different coprime exponents, without padding. Recover the flag without factoring n.
hint: Use extended Euclid to find a·e1+b·e2=1. Negative powers require modular inverses.

title: Lost in the log
summary: An unusual line in an ordinary shift report.
description: Search the provided operations log for the flag. No external systems are involved.
hint: A text search for FALCON is enough.

title: The attachment
summary: The message is plain. Its attachment is not.
description: An archived email contains a small attachment. Extract it and read the flag.
hint: MIME attachments often use Base64 transfer encoding.

title: Out of order
summary: A transfer arrived in scattered pieces.
description: Reassemble the DNS transfer from packet-summary records. Only queries under transfer.falcon.invalid belong to this session. Sort by the numeric sequence label, concatenate the next label, then Base64-decode.
hint: The sequence numbers are hexadecimal, not decimal.

title: Beneath the sand
summary: A deleted record survives inside a binary fragment.
description: Carve a record from the supplied disk fragment. Record format: ASCII FFARCHIVE, NUL, four ASCII decimal length digits, then that many payload bytes. The payload is Base64.
hint: Search for the signature as bytes; do not treat the entire fragment as text.

title: Blue hour
summary: The quietest bits carry the message.
description: A 24-bit BMP contains a hidden record in the least significant bit of each blue byte, in on-disk pixel order. Bits are MSB-first within a byte. The first decoded byte is the payload length.
hint: Read the pixel-data offset from the BMP header. Blue is the first byte of each BGR pixel.

title: Fragmented flight
summary: Retransmissions and a second stream obscure the evidence.
description: Reconstruct stream 7 using TCP sequence numbers from this exported packet capture. Ignore other streams, remove retransmitted bytes, and treat sequence numbers as unsigned integers. The reconstructed bytes contain the flag.
hint: Place each byte at sequence−minimum_sequence; duplicate packets must not duplicate content.

title: Readable secrets
summary: The program says more than its output.
description: Inspect the supplied Python source to recover the flag. Running it is optional.
hint: Look at the variable names, not just the printed message.

title: Backwards glance
summary: A small transformation hides a familiar format.
description: The checker compares your input after reversing it. Recover the original input.
hint: Reverse the target string.

title: Byte dance
summary: Every byte takes one step and a turn.
description: Reverse the byte transformation in the checker. Input and output bytes are in the range 0–255.
hint: Undo XOR first, then subtract the index-dependent offset modulo 256.

title: Turn the wheel
summary: Bit rotations are hiding behind an innocent checker.
description: Invert the checker to recover the flag. The rotation operates on eight-bit unsigned values.
hint: Undo rotate-left by rotating right three bits, then undo XOR.

title: Chain reaction
summary: Each byte depends on the one before it.
description: A stateful checker combines each input byte with internal state. Recover the full accepted input.
hint: The stored output reveals the new state after XOR. Use the previous state to recover each input byte.

title: Tiny machine
summary: An unfamiliar instruction set guards the final transmission.
description: Analyze the included virtual machine and its bytecode to reconstruct its output. Write an emulator or trace it. The program performs no network or filesystem operations.
hint: Opcode 1 pushes, 2 subtracts, 3 XORs, and 4 emits the top of the stack.

title: View from the source
summary: The visible page is only half the story.
description: Download and inspect this offline HTML page. The developer left a flag in a comment.
hint: Use View Source or open the downloaded file in a text editor.

title: Cookie crumbs
summary: Encoding never made a cookie private.
description: An offline HTTP response contains a session cookie. Recover the flag stored inside it. No live service is involved.
hint: The cookie value is Base64-encoded JSON.

title: Signed, not hidden
summary: A signature leaves the contents readable.
description: Inspect the supplied demonstration JWT. Recover the internal flag from its payload. You do not need to forge a token or know a signing key.
hint: JWT segments use Base64URL; the payload is the middle segment.

title: A map to nowhere
summary: A forgotten source map reveals the original code.
description: The supplied production source map includes embedded source text. Find the internal flag.
hint: Inspect sourcesContent. A source map can ship original code even when production JavaScript is minified.

title: Conflicting boundaries
summary: Two parsers disagree about where a message ends.
description: Study the offline HTTP trace. The frontend honors Content-Length, while the backend honors Transfer-Encoding: chunked. Extract the body of the second request seen by the backend. It is the flag. CRLF line endings are used. Do not send this trace to any server.
hint: The backend ends the first body at 0 CRLF CRLF; the next POST begins a second request.

title: Cache key collision
summary: One normalization step changes which response survives.
description: Analyze this offline cache simulation. Determine the URL that collides with /internal/flag after cache-key normalization but passes the edge path check. Then use that exact URL as the repeating XOR key to decrypt the supplied ciphertext. The intended URL contains one parent-directory segment. No live endpoint exists.
hint: The edge checks the original path. The cache resolves .. segments. Try /public/../internal/flag as the XOR key.
